  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor (5 levels). Given the extreme right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81), consider log-transformation or robust ANOVA. The large SD relative to mean and extreme max value suggest heavy-tailed distribution.",
    "Success: Binary outcome (0/1) with mean 0.73. Standard ANOVA inappropriate due to binary nature. Use logistic regression or generalized linear model with binomial family and logit link. Report odds ratios relative to Sham reference.",
    "Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Extremely right-skewed (max=29.82 vs mean=0.47) with values bounded [0,1] theoretically but data shows supra-unity values indicating calculation artifacts or unbounded metric. Consider log-transformation, rank-based ANOVA, or gamma GLM.",
    "Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Moderate right skew (max=75.35 vs mean=12.50). Consider robust ANOVA or Welch's ANOVA if variance heterogeneity detected.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Bounded [0,1] with mean 0.38, SD 0.24. Beta regression or arcsine-square-root transformation recommended due to bounded nature; standard ANOVA may produce predictions outside valid range."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Assumed via experimental design; verify no temporal autocorrelation within mice using Durbin-Watson or autocorrelation function on residuals.",
    "Normality: Shapiro-Wilk or Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests on residuals for each response; Q-Q plots mandatory given extreme skewness in Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test for equality of variances across 5 paradigms; Brown-Forsythe if normality violated. Given unequal sample sizes (Combined n=48846 vs Bright Visual Only n=3323), variance heterogeneity likely problematic.",
    "Sample size imbalance: Combined paradigm dominates (63.7% of data). Weighted analyses or hierarchical models with mouse-level random effects recommended to handle imbalance and non-independence.",
    "Outlier assessment: Identify extreme values (Time-to-Target >20s, Path Efficiency >5) for sensitivity analyses; document influence on ANOVA results."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus test significant for continuous responses: Tukey HSD for pairwise comparisons with familywise error control, or Games-Howell if variance heterogeneity confirmed.",
    "For Success (logistic regression): pairwise odds ratios with Bonferroni-Holm correction for 10 comparisons (5 choose 2).",
    "Focus contrasts: Combined vs each single-modality condition (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only) to test multisensory enhancement; each active condition vs Sham to establish efficacy.",
    "Effect sizes: Eta-squared or partial eta-squared for ANOVA; Cohen's d for pairwise comparisons; odds ratios for Success.",
    "Visualization: Boxplots with jittered points or violin plots given sample sizes; mean ± 95% CI plots for clarity with large N."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Combined paradigm likely shows fastest Time-to-Target and highest Success given largest sample size and presumed optimization in experimental design.",
    "ICMS Only and Visual-only paradigms may show intermediate performance; uncertainty about whether Dim vs Bright Visual differ substantially.",
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance (highest Time-to-Target, lowest Success, lowest Path Efficiency) serving as baseline.",
    "AD (angular dispersion) may differentiate paradigms with tighter trajectories (lower AD) in effective stimulation conditions.",
    "Path Efficiency and Average Speed relationships may be complex due to speed-accuracy tradeoffs; high speed with low efficiency possible in some conditions."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe sample size imbalance: Combined (48846) vs Bright Visual Only (3323) creates 14.7:1 ratio, reducing power for comparisons involving smaller groups and potentially biasing variance estimates.",
    "Single-factor analysis ignores Mouse as blocking factor; 8 mice with unequal trials (7233-10986) introduce potential confounding if mouse-stimulation assignment not fully crossed.",
    "Success as binary outcome violates ANOVA assumptions; logistic regression required but not explicitly requested in prompt template.",
    "Path Efficiency values >1 suggest metric calculation differs from standard straight-line/actual-path ratio; interpretation uncertain.",
    "No temporal information: Cannot assess learning effects or session effects that may interact with stimulation paradigm.",
    "Temperature=0.0 and model=kimi with summary_only data view provides no access to raw trial-level data for diagnostic plotting or model validation.",
    "Extreme outliers in Time-to-Target (max 201.4s, ~100x median) and Path Efficiency (max 29.8) may disproportionately influence means; medians and robust statistics more appropriate."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect for Time-to-Target, log-transformed Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and arcsine-sqrt(AD); use generalized linear mixed model (GLMM) with binomial family for Success. This addresses non-independence, sample imbalance, and provides paradigm-specific estimates with 95% confidence intervals. Follow with estimated marginal means and pairwise contrasts with Tukey adjustment."
}
